proposals.evidence: The whole predicate consists of thirst + lag- be felt/strike. Turner 5936 documents Hindi tis, Punjabi tīh and Gujarati taras in the tṛṣā family; 10895 documents regional lāg- be felt/touch/begin. The past and infinitival endings belong to the modern lag- paradigm, rather than adding an independent auxiliary. Both ordered lexical constituents are represented; reduced tar/tas forms and clauses with additional copulas are excluded.

proposals.evidence: The full predicate is hunger + be felt/strike. Turner bubhukṣā lists Hindi bhūk(h), Old Marwari bhūkha, Oriya bhuk(h)a/bhoka and Jaunsari bhukh; lagyati supplies the matching regional lag-/lāg- paradigm, including Oriya lāgibā and western Pahari be felt. These responses contain two lexical constituents, with local tense/person/infinitive endings retained; clauses with additional copulas or progressive auxiliaries are excluded.
